input.prompt:
A candid, casual photo taken on an iPhone 15 Pro by a traveller at a small hillside café in Old Manali, Himachal Pradesh. Looks like a real, unedited personal Instagram post, not an advertisement and not a studio shot. Natural phone-camera look: slight HDR from the phone, a little digital noise in the shadows, imperfect framing tilted maybe 2 degrees, focus on the bottle.

PRODUCT — the real Spraymax bottle from the reference photos: a white plastic 100 ml spray bottle (slightly greyish, semi-matte white like the real bottle in the hand-held reference photo, not a perfect glossy render), white ribbed screw collar and spray pump, clear plastic overcap with a few fingerprints and light scuffs. Front label exactly as in the references: "Spraymax" printed vertically in deep indigo rounded letters, the small line "Instant Hair Volume & Texture", and a dark blue ocean-wave photo band at the bottom with "FOR ALL HAIR TYPES" and "100ml/3.38fl.oz." The label is a paper sticker with slightly visible edges. Faithful letterforms and colors, no other text on the bottle.

SCENE: the bottle stands on the flat top of an old, weathered wooden café railing — sun-faded, cracked deodar wood with chipped paint and a few scratches. Next to it, slightly behind and to the left, a small glass of half-finished masala chai (cutting chai glass) with a tea stain ring on the wood. A pair of cheap sunglasses lies folded near the edge. Behind the railing, slightly out of focus: a green valley with tall deodar pine trees, a few old slate-roofed village houses on the slope, a faded string of Tibetan prayer flags crossing part of the frame, and in the far distance snow-dusted Himalayan peaks partly covered by soft clouds.

LIGHT: late afternoon, soft hazy daylight with a light overcast, gentle natural shadows, true colors, nothing glowing or overly dramatic, no studio lighting.

COMPOSITION: vertical 4:5, bottle slightly right of center in the lower half, roughly a third of the frame height, shot from about chest height a little above the railing. Background naturally soft but still recognisable (phone portrait-mode style). Some open sky and clouds near the top.

STRICTLY: no people, no hands, no fingers. No added text, captions, watermarks, logos or graphics anywhere except the bottle's own label. Everyday imperfection is good — dust, wood grain, uneven light — avoid anything that looks perfectly arranged, symmetrical, CGI or overly polished.
